newsitem.title: USA: Florida Progress net hurt by utility costs.
newsitem.headline: Florida Progress net hurt by utility costs.

text.p: Florida Progress Corp on Thursday reported lower first quarter earnings citing increased utility expenses and floods on the Ohio and Mississippi rivers.
The company said earnings declined to $0.43 per share from $0.50 in 1996's initial quarter. Revenues, however, rose to $747.5 million from $730.4 million last year.

Increased operating and maintenance expenses for Florida Power Corp accounted for some of the reduced earnings, the company said. These expenses were almost $10 million higher compared with the first quarter of 1996.

The increase was due primarily to costs associated with the outage of the Crystal River nuclear plant and several fossil plant outages. The nuclear unit is scheduled to be out of service until year-end 1997 while modifications required by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission are made to several of the unit's backup safety systems.

Lower preferred stock dividends and depreciation expense helped to offset some of these higher expenses. In 1996, Florida Power redeemed $105 million in preferred stock, which reduced preferred dividends by about $2 million. Depreciation of regulatory assets was accelerated in 1996, which lowered depreciation expense by approximately $3 million in 1997.
Earnings of Electric Fuels Corp, the energy and transportation subsidiary of Florida Progress, dropped to $3.3 million in the latest quarter from $6.8 million last year.

The company said the decrease is attributable to adverse weather and flooding along the Ohio and Mississippi rivers, which damaged company-owned terminal facilities and continues to disrupt river traffic.
